tasks.short: Read care labels and examine each article, sort articles into lots, tag them with the customer's ticket number and note stains and damage.

steps.what: Laundry worker reads care labels and examines articles to be cleaned
Laundry worker sorts articles into lots by color, fabric, dirt content and cleaning technique
Laundry worker tags each article with the ticket number: written by hand today; after the change the counter system prints a barcode tag from the order and the worker attaches it
Laundry worker notes stains and damage: on the paper ticket today, on the article's record on a tablet after the change

tasks.design: The counter system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) prints a barcode tag per article from the customer's order, and the worker notes stains and damage on the article's record on a tablet with a photo, so they are on record before cleaning; the note is still the worker's own record. Examining and sorting stay with the worker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tags and damage notes were written by hand on paper tickets.
tasks.enabler_now: Counter systems for dry cleaners print barcode tags and store notes and photos per article.
tasks.still_hard: Sorting depends on feel and experience; labels are often missing or wrong.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting that a 'washable' label is wrong for this silk.

reach.learn: Whether photos at intake cut damage disputes.

evidence.claim: Counter systems for dry cleaners print barcode tags and store notes and photos per article.
Customer tickets hold names and phone numbers, so personal data rules apply.

assumptions: Boundary: from incoming articles to sorted lots; cleaning is outside.
Input contract: orders taken at the counter by the counter assistant; fallback is paper tickets.
Examining, sorting and noting damage keep their full time; a tap is no faster than a pen. s3 keeps 60 for printing and attaching each tag.
Industrial linen with fixed tags is outside this design.
research_questions: Do lost or mixed-up articles fall?

incremental.description: Laundry worker takes photos of damaged articles.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half of the orders still come on paper tickets, so half of the tags are written by hand (1.5); high: orders taken in the counter system as assumed (3.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Identify the fabric and stain, look up the spotting procedure, choose the procedure and solvent, test it on a hidden spot and note the treatment.

steps.what: Laundry worker identifies the fabric and stain type
Laundry worker looks up the spotting chart in the supplier's manual
Laundry worker determines spotting procedures and proper solvents
Laundry worker tests the solvent on a hidden spot
Laundry worker records the treatment used: on the ticket today, on the article's record in the counter system after the change

tasks.design: The supplier's spotting chart is put on a tablet at the spotting board ({OTHER}) as a table filtered by fabric and stain, with the solvent's safety sheet one tap away. The worker records the treatment used on the article's record in the counter system ({OPS_SYSTEM}). Identifying, choosing, testing and spotting stay with the worker; no AI advises.
tasks.previous_blocker: Charts were in a binder at the board and treatments written on tickets.
tasks.enabler_now: Tablets at the workstation can show filtered charts and record picks per article.
tasks.still_hard: Unknown stains and mixed fabrics still need experience and a test.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing a stain is old wine, not coffee, by its edge.

reach.learn: Whether a filtered chart speeds up learning.

evidence.claim: Spotting charts from chemical suppliers match stain and fabric types to agents and steps.
Safety data sheets for solvents must be available to the workers who use them.

assumptions: Boundary: from the stained article to the treatment note; cleaning is outside.
Input contract: spotting chart from the chemical supplier; fallback is the binder.
Identifying, choosing, testing and recording the treatment keep their full time; the record is a first write. s2 keeps 50 for reading the filtered chart.
The chart is updated when the supplier changes products.

already_counted.description: Laundry worker reads the filtered chart.

incremental.description: No ongoing upkeep for the worker: recording the treatment is step s5, and the chart is updated with the supplier's products.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many stains are unknown or mixed fabrics outside the chart, so half of the lookups still use the binder (5.0); high: the filtered chart covers most stains (10.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The laundry worker keeps examining, sorting and spotting; handwritten tags, notes and binder look-ups shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A laundry where every article's history is on record from intake to pickup.
